lower_bound.quote:
Having fewer edges than vertices, the graph contains
no cycle and no loop, since a cycle or a loop on \(v\) vertices already uses at
least \(v\) edges; hence every connected component \(C\) has \(e_C=v_C-1\) and
is a tree (an isolated vertex counts as a tree).
lower_bound.witness: Counterexample: take q=2 with a_1=1/10 and a_2=9/10, and make one cut splitting a_2 into pieces 1/2 and 2/5. The sorted pieces are (1/2,2/5,1/10). The sole rank-pair consists of two pieces from vertex 2, so its edge is a loop. Thus the graph has one edge on two vertices, satisfying 1≤q−1 and having fewer edges than vertices, but it contains a loop; moreover the component containing a_q=a_2 is not a tree and cannot be bipartitioned as asserted.
lower_bound.load_bearing: The tree claim is used to obtain the bipartition and inequality (3), which are the entire proof of D≥Γ for every Xiang refinement. The matching lower bound invokes precisely this unproved half of the refinement lemma.

parsed.notes: The closed form is correct. The drafting reduction and Xiang construction are valid, but the all-n Liu bound relies on a false graph-acyclicity inference.
